title: Occupational Biomechanics Tool Entry
description: Metadata record for one entry in the Tools library: usable analysis software or instrumentation, commercial or free. Aligned with schema.org/SoftwareApplication. The library links out; it does not rehost or resell anything. Distinct from the Models library, whose entries are anchored on a publication.

id.description: Unique slug, also the filename. Lowercase, hyphenated.

sample.description: true for placeholder/example entries. Remove or set false for real records.

vendor.description: Company or organization that sells or distributes the tool, e.g. 'NexGen Ergonomics'.

source.description: Who developed the tool and where, when known (often a lab behind the commercial product).

links.description: At least one outbound link. website is the vendor's product page.

paper.description: Publication describing or validating the tool, usually https://doi.org/...

record.description: Institutional or project page, e.g. a university lab site.

licensing.description: How the tool is obtained: commercial = paid license; free = no-cost but closed; open_source = code available under an open license.

pricing_note.description: One line on licensing terms, e.g. 'via NexGen Ergonomics; ~$10k/yr academic consortium option'.

patents.description: Patents protecting the tool, when known.

url.description: Patent record, e.g. a Google Patents page.

category.description: What kind of tool, e.g. 'Video task analysis'.

inputs.description: What the tool consumes, e.g. 'Conventional workplace video'.

outputs.description: What the tool produces, e.g. 'Time-study reports, duty cycle'.

related_models.description: ids of Models-library entries the tool implements or builds on.

related_datasets.description: ids of catalog datasets collected or analyzed with the tool.
